novelty_flags.label: thm:affine-ensemble-inference
novelty_flags.one_line: Efficiency of the advertised estimator is conditional on the directly assumed L2 convergence to the efficient signal, so the construction has not yet derived an attaining estimator from primitive model and learner conditions.

soundness_flags.label: def:joint-model; ass:locally-constant-rank; ass:moving-kernel-continuity
soundness_flags.one_line: Membership and the score set depend on an unquantified path P_t, so it is unclear whether the rank/projection clauses restrict every admissible local path, one selected path, or a separately defined rank-chart model.

soundness_flags.label: target_estimand; sampling_model
soundness_flags.one_line: The core calls theta a causal proximal ATE but supplies only observed bridge restrictions; it lacks the latent negative-control/proxy assumptions that identify this observed functional with E[Y(1)-Y(0)].

soundness_flags.label: thm:affine-ensemble-inference
soundness_flags.one_line: The theorem's asserted feasible attainment relies on the undeveloped premise that the named learned affine signal already converges to theta+phi_eff, rather than on conditions connected to the stated bridge and Galerkin learners.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: oeq:score-lifting-completeness and all explicitly conditional downstream theorems
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: General tangent completeness is an unresolved, explicitly named Stage-0 obligation.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The global quotient-efficiency, attainment, and general inference claims are assessed only conditional on proving T_P=C_P^perp; the finite-chart witness remains an independent local result.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 10-13, Lemma 1, Theorems 2-3; pp. 24-27, proofs of Theorems 2-3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The negative-control observed model is characterized by the outcome-bridge moment alone; Theorem 3 gives an ATE efficient influence function and variance bound via a generalized inverse, without a separate treatment-bridge-existence restriction.
Under unique h and q with surjective T and T-prime, Theorem 3.1 gives the familiar proximal efficient influence function.

The published article concerns nonunique integral-equation solutions and states root-n regular, asymptotically semiparametrically locally efficient inference under additional regularity; theorem-level primary text was inaccessible for further formula comparison.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author manuscript corresponding to Journal of Econometrics 170(2), 2012
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives efficiency bounds for identified linear functionals when the NPIV structural regression may be underidentified or ill-posed, using Hilbert-space range and projection geometry.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define M_joint as an explicit local rank-chart model, quantify its admissible Hellinger paths, and state whether treatment-bridge existence is a submanifold restriction; then prove the finite witness is relatively open in that exact model.

Add a theorem-level algebraic comparison with Chen-Xie's Theorem 3 that identifies precisely which normal directions arise from treatment-bridge existence and proves a strict variance improvement on the displayed chart.

Replace the assumed efficient-signal L2 convergence in the ensemble theorem with primitive sieve approximation, bridge-learning, Gram-stability, and weight-error conditions sufficient for that convergence.
Either add the latent negative-control assumptions needed for causal ATE interpretation or consistently relabel theta as an observed bridge functional.

recommended_next_step: Revise the statistical model and causal scope first, then establish a direct strict comparison to Chen-Xie and a primitive learner theorem before advancing to Stage 0.
